phases.title: Before the first line
phases.goal: Know what is being ported, where it comes from, how others did such a thing, and how this project will work. Every step is an explainer.

steps.title: The workflow and the repo
steps.what: How Pietro has been working with nimib and AI, and this site made accordingly: devlog, review mode, the look, roadmap, coverage map, CI.

steps.title: Gleam, its people and its programs
steps.what: The language, how it is used, the projects big and small, the people, and the house rules a port should respect.

steps.title: Where Gleam's decisions live
steps.what: No specification and no RFCs: a ranked map of where design decisions are written down, and a recipe to look one up.

steps.title: A corpus of real Gleam
steps.what: Seventy five projects pinned at exact commits with their licences (corpus/corpus.json), and the tool that pins, fetches and measures them.

steps.title: The BEAM and Erlang
steps.what: A short history, what it solves, how a language is built on it, how Gleam lives on it.

steps.title: Elm, the other root
steps.what: Its history and principles, the type system, developer experience, and what Gleam took from it.

steps.title: The compiler, taken apart, and the plan
steps.what: How compilers are made and how Gleam's is; its history; the components, the order to port them, which backend first, how each step is verified.

steps.title: Other rewrites
steps.what: How a big project is rewritten in another language, by people and by AI: what worked, what did not, what to copy.

steps.title: How to develop
steps.what: Specs, decision records, tooling to verify the port and tooling for Pietro to review it.

phases.title: The front end
phases.goal: Gleam source in, a tree out, the same tree the Rust compiler builds. The plan thread fills in this phase and the next ones.

steps.title: The lexer
steps.what: Source text to tokens: the first piece of the compiler in Nim, checked token by token against the Rust lexer.
